newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-French franc rallies on mark with EMU hopes.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-French franc rallies on mark with EMU hopes.

text.p: The French franc surged to a two- month high against the mark on Friday as the markets turned bullish on the future of monetary union and European finance ministers gathered in Dublin.

This weekend's Dublin meeting comes amid an intense scramble by EU governments to bring their 1997 budget deficits in line with Maastricht treaty criteria for European economic and monetary union (EMU).
"The EMU theme is dominant in the forex market, and anything that's good for EMU is bad for the mark," said Giorgio Radaelli, international economist at Lehman Brothers.
"The mark is generally weak on the crosses, but it was the surging French franc that grabbed the market's attention," commented Philippe Delmotte, a trader at Bank of Boston.
Analysts said the volume of franc-mark trades had been huge, perhaps three times higher than dollar-mark, which normally sees the bulk of foreign exchange trade.

"The move today is an adjunct to the ECOFIN meeting in Dublin and as the Franco-German determination on EMU becomes clearer, all the long-term risks point downward for the mark," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN Amro in London.

"First German interest rates are almost certainly not going to rise within the next six months and its now pretty clear the Franco-German axis is not going to tolerate any significant appreciation of the mark," he added.
At 1545 GMT the franc was at 3.3885 to the mark -- around two centimes stronger than its level late in Europe on Thursday.
The weaker mark also saw the dollar rise to two-month highs of 1.5186 marks before profit-taking pulled it back to around 1.5148 by 1545 GMT.

Generally speaking, dealers said, interest rate jitters were still overhanging dollar trades, with the main topic of conversation being next week's U.S. rate-setting Federal Open Markets Committee meeting. Many analysts expect a 25 basis point (quarter percent) rise in the Fed funds rate.
On the European bourses, volatile London shares retreated sharply from an opening rally which took them to a new record peak. London's blue chip FTSE closed down about a quarter percent at 3964.1.
Analysts said the morning rally, which saw the FTSE index jump to a record 3,994.1 had been related to a futures and options expiry.

The quarterly futures and options expiry is important because market players have to decide whether to take any profits or losses on their positions or to "roll over," or take new positions, in the next contract period.

The expiry is often associated with unusually high levels of market volatility as traders and investors bet on market moves through the next three months, using derivatives which often set the pace for the rest of the stock market.

German shares ended bourse trade near a new record high set earlier. They were also led up by trade spilling over from futures expiries. The DAX 30-share index closed 21.66 points up at 2,646.10, just off A record intra-day high of 2,650.49.

But French shares had traded in negative territory for most of the day but pared some of their losses to close only about three points down. Earlier commercial banks cut base lending rates by 20 basis points to 6.55 percent and investors, who had been expecting such a move, took profits on the last day of what they called a good week.
On the precious metals market, silver slumped in nervous trading after an overnight sell-off sent prices spiralling below the key $5.00 an ounce level.
"It broke through an important trend line going back three years last night and that's knocked the confidence out of the market quite a lot," a dealer said.
CURRENCIES AT 1545 GMT
The dollar was at 1.5148 marks and 109.83 yen compared with 1.5139 marks and 109.40 yen in Europe late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS
The Financial Times-Stock Exchange index of 100 leading British shares ended 10.2 points lower at 3,964.1.
In Paris, the CAC-40 share index finished down 2.87 at 2,079.46.
The 30-share DAX index in Frankfurt closed up 21.66 at 2,646.10. In post bourse trade the IBIS DAX index was up 16.04 at 2,641.50. PRECIOUS METALS
Gold closed at $381.75, compared with its close in London on Thursday of $382.85.
